newsitem.title: POLAND: SAMSUNG READY TO IMPROVE BID TO BUY POLISH BANK.
newsitem.headline: SAMSUNG READY TO IMPROVE BID TO BUY POLISH BANK.

text.p: South Korean Samsung Group said on Friday it was ready to improve its offer to buy a 65 percent stake of Polish state-owned Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK).

The group, whose subsidiary Samsung Life Insurance is bidding for PBK against a Polish consortium, said in a statement it would buy 51 percent of PBK and later purchase 14 percent at market price within two years at the option of the treasury.
Samsung earlier wanted to buy PBK's 65 percent at a fixed price.
The group said it thought the government privileged the offer of the Polish consortium of Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy BPH, Kredyt Bank and insurer Warta.

"While Samsung certainly does not question the Polish government's inherent rights to privatise its state-owned enterprises...we would question the integrity of the authorities who are attempting to hide what appears to be a predetermined selection of the so-called Polish consortium behind a claimed free and open tender process," the statement said.
The government said it had put off its choice of an investor for PBK until its session next week. The selection was earlier postponed several times.
Government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowski said the delay was necessary, because Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz had asked the treasury about the details of the sale.

A source close to the government said the prime minister wanted to know why the treasury ministry wanted to sell a stake in PBK to a Polish consortium rather than to Samsung, even though the latter had offered a better price for the bank.
"The prime minister has asked why an offer that envisages a worse price has been chosen," the source, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
The government plans to float another 15 percent of PBK on the Warsaw bourse and the bank's issue prospectus was submitted to the Securities Commission last week.
HSBC Investment Services, which is advising the government on the privatisation, said the stake was likely to hit the bourse in October.
It estimated the bank's total value at between 1.2 billion zlotys and 1.6 billion zlotys ($366.7-$489 million).
